subject.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write

question: Should config writes expose comment-loss information through the new optional ConfigWriteResult.warning contract, or should this warning remain an internal diagnostic without expanding the exported result shape?
rationale: Both designs can warn before data loss, but selecting the permanent central config-writer contract affects callers and upgrade compatibility and therefore requires owner intent.

options.title: Keep structured warning
options.body: Remove the duplicate type declaration, retain the optional warning result, and prove existing root/include callers plus quiet-output paths remain compatible.

options.title: Keep warning internal
options.body: Emit the pre-write diagnostic through the existing logging path without adding a new exported result field, preserving the current caller contract.

options.title: Pause for preservation design
options.body: Defer this mitigation and design a broader comment-preserving config writer, accepting substantially larger implementation and migration scope.

recommendation.title: Keep structured warning
recommendation.body: Remove the duplicate type declaration, retain the optional warning result, and prove existing root/include callers plus quiet-output paths remain compatible.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person most directly to recent central config IO, migration, validation, and documentation work.
